# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute: my only channel is gestures, and only Deaf can see them. That makes Deaf my translator — whatever I learn must flow through Deaf's voice to Blind, who is the only one who can cut. The chain is: me → gesture → Deaf → speech → Blind. Nobody else can carry my manual to the one pair of hands.

What I know that nobody else does: printed markings on the bomb are bait — acting on them detonates us — and the real rule is the light-color table (blue light → cut yellow, green → green, red → blue). The immediate danger is Deaf cheerfully reading the printed labels aloud to Blind as if they were instructions. So my first priority is to stamp "print = lie" before Deaf relays anything.

I have no shared code yet, so I'm seeding one from the most guessable symbols: 👋 attention, 👉 "that thing over there" (the bomb), ✍ anything written, 👎 no/false, 👍 yes/true. My two critical lessons: "the bomb's print is false," then "the light is true." Then ✋ (stop — nobody touches anything yet; there is no timer, so patience costs nothing and a wrong cut costs everything) and 🫴 (an open palm: give me — I'm asking Deaf to report aloud, since Deaf can speak and I can hear; whatever Deaf says lands on me at the start of next round).

The plan after that: once Deaf describes what they see — the light's color and where each wire sits — I can answer next round with position gestures (👈 👉 👆 👇) instead of color words, which Blind can verify by touch. We confirm in plain speech before Blind cuts anything.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👉", "✍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫰", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands find, exactly: one large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE; one display, whose contents I cannot feel; one light, whose state I cannot perceive; three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, and I feel no colors on any of them. I will not push or cut until the manual tells me to. Important: I cannot see gestures, so I can never receive anything from you directly. Only speech reaches me, and only Deaf can be my voice. Please sign to Deaf everything I just reported, plus whatever the manual needs to know. Then have Deaf speak me the wire colors in order 1 to 3, what the display shows, and the light's color, followed by the manual's instruction. I am also waving to Deaf right now as a channel check.
Deaf says: Hello Mute and Blind, Deaf here. I see the bomb and I cannot hear anything at all, so I will never hear your replies. Full bomb report: the display shows the number 0. The light is blue. There is one large button printed with PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. That is every module and every marking on it. I will announce at once if the display changes.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your three signed messages but we had no shared code yet, so let us fix one now — I am making each sign as I name it. Numbers: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖐 four, ✋ five. 👍 yes, 👎 no. Parts: 👊 the button, 👆 the display, 👌 the light, 🤞 the wires. Actions: ✊ press, 🤏 cut, 🫳 hold down, 🫴 release, ✍ type or enter. To point at a wire, make the wires sign then its number. Example: cut wire two is 🤏 ✌. Your raised hand with the open palm looked like give me everything — the full report above is everything there is. Remember: Blind can hear speech, so anything you need Blind to know, just say it aloud and they hear you directly, but I will not — I only see gestures. Send every defusal instruction to me as signs and I will relay it to Blind word for word.

What just happened: I can hear, Deaf cannot — so Deaf's public report reached me in full. The bomb: display 0, light BLUE, wires 1=blue 2=green 3=yellow, and a button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. My manual keys everything off the light: blue light → cut the yellow wire → that is wire 3. The button's embossed label is exactly the "print as bait" my manual warns about — it must never be pressed, and the display's number is to be ignored too.

Deaf built a sign code and labelled it aloud while signing, so I now hold the full vocabulary: numbers ☝✌🤟🖐✋, yes/no 👍👎, parts 👊👆👌🤞, actions ✊🤏🫳🫴✍, wire-pointing as 🤞+number. I will abandon my round-one guesses and adopt Deaf's code exclusively.

The immediate, unambiguous instruction — cut wire three (🤏 🤟) — I send first in pure established code, so Deaf can relay it to Blind even before decoding anything else. Around it: 👊👎 (never press the button), ✍👎 (what is printed/displayed is false), 👌👍🤞👍 (the light and the wire colours are the true inputs).

The gap in Deaf's code is colours, and I cannot speak new signs into existence — Deaf must decode them. So I use the bomb itself as a Rosetta stone: I pair each wire's number with a fresh sign (🤞☝🫱, 🤞✌🫲, 🤞🤟🤙), then sign the light with 🫱 — the same sign as wire one, which the light visibly matches right now (both blue). That gives Deaf a unique consistent solution plus a built-in check. With colours named, I can send the whole table so Deaf's relay stays correct even if the light changes: blue→cut 3, green→cut 2, red→cut 1. Finally a gate: only cut while the light is still blue; if it changes, hands off until my next signs — Blind speaks before Deaf each round, so no cut can happen without Deaf relaying first, and I get a fresh turn before anything irreversible.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍", "🤞", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🤏", "🤞", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "☝", "🫱", "🤞", "✌", "🫲", "🤞", "🤟", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫱"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫱", "🤏", "🤞", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫲", "🤏", "🤞", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫵", "🤏", "🤞", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫱", "👍", "🤏", "🤞", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫱", "👎", "🤏", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: Deaf's visual report reached me — display 0, light blue, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. I am holding still. Please sign Deaf the manual rules now, word for word and completely: everything about the button module, what the display number and the light color mean, and every rule about cutting the blue, green and yellow wires, including order and how many. State each rule as a condition: if the display shows X, do Y; if the light is Z, do W. One safety check first: Deaf numbered the wires by sight, but if we stand on opposite sides, left and right are mirrored for one of us. Ask Deaf to anchor the numbering to the bomb itself — for example, whether wire 1 is the one nearest the display, nearest the light, or nearest the button. Tell me the landmark and the answer through Deaf's voice, and only then give me the cutting order. Until Deaf speaks the instruction to me directly, my hands stay off everything.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, read-back of your signs, using our code: button — do not press. Keypad — do not type. Rule from the manual: light blue means cut wire three; light green means cut wire two; light yellow means cut wire one. Our light IS blue, so I am ordering the cut of wire three. Two questions first: does the display showing zero require anything at all, or is it ignored? And is wire three found by its printed number, so Blind must identify it by position? If anything I have said is wrong, then in your very next turn SPEAK ALOUD to Blind before they act — your spoken words reach them in time to stop the cut, but your signs to me arrive only after. If everything is right, just signal me 👍.

Deaf's read-back is close, and the critical part survived: blue→cut 3, green→cut 2 are decoded correctly, and Deaf has already ordered the wire-3 cut. But three things need handling before Blind's hands move. First, the mirror problem Blind raised is real: "wire 3" by sight could be wire 1 from the other side, and cutting the blue wire under a blue light detonates us. Anchoring must come first, so I am not sending the bare 👍 Deaf asked for. Second, Deaf decoded my third light-state sign 🫵 as "yellow," but it is the red-light rule; since wire 3's colour sign was 🤙, I am re-sending the wire-colour Rosetta so the collision surfaces in Deaf's read-back. Deaf will see red aloud if it ever appears, so the mismatch self-corrects with one lost round at worst. Third, Deaf believes I can "speak aloud" to Blind as a fallback. I cannot — I am the Mute; Deaf is the only voice Blind will ever hear, which makes Deaf's relay accuracy load-bearing. Meanwhile I answer Deaf's two questions: the display's 0 is bait like all print, and wires are numbered by sight, not by any printed label. I introduce 🤌 as a question marker for the landmark query — Deaf invents and adopts signs readily, and their read-back loop will catch any misdecode while Blind holds still.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎", "🤞", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫱", "🤏", "🤞", "🤟", "👍", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🫲", "🤏", "🤞", "✌", "👍"])
